pages.title: The Woman Who Touched the Cloak
retelling: A big crowd was following Jesus. They pushed and squeezed to get close to him.
In the crowd was a woman who had been sick for twelve years. All her money had gone on doctors, but she only got worse.
The woman had heard about Jesus. “If I can just touch his clothes,” she thought, “I will be well.”
She crept up behind Jesus and touched his cloak. At once she felt strong and well again.
Jesus stopped. “Who touched my clothes?” he asked. His friends said, “Look at all these people! How can you ask who touched you?” But Jesus kept looking around.
The woman was shaking with fear. She came and knelt in front of Jesus, and she told him everything.
Jesus was not cross. He spoke kindly to her. “Daughter,” he said, “you trusted me, and now you are well. Go in peace.”
pages.message: Jesus is never too busy for us. When we trust him and come close, he cares for us.

questions.q: How long had the woman been sick?
What did the woman touch, and where was she standing?
questions.a: She touched Jesus' cloak. She was behind him in the crowd.

questions.q: The woman was afraid, but she still came to Jesus. When have you felt shy about asking for help? Who could you ask?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk, then remind them that they can always talk to Jesus, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Hold the corner of a cloth and say, “Thank you, Jesus, for noticing me.” Then say hello to someone who is often left out.

pages.title: The Soldier and His Servant
retelling: In the town of Capernaum lived a Roman soldier. He was an officer, and a hundred soldiers took orders from him.
The officer had a servant he cared about very much. The servant was very sick, and he was close to dying.
The officer heard that Jesus was nearby. He asked some Jewish leaders to go and ask Jesus for help.
Jesus set off with them. But before he reached the house, the officer sent some friends with a message.
“Lord, you do not need to come inside,” they said. “I am not good enough to have you in my home. Only say the word, and my servant will get well.”
The officer knew about orders. When he told a soldier to go, the soldier went. He believed Jesus could give an order to sickness too.
Jesus was amazed. He turned to the crowd. “I have not found anyone with faith as big as this,” he said.
The friends went back to the house. The servant was well again!
pages.message: Jesus has power to help, and we can trust his word. He is glad when we believe him.

questions.q: What was the matter with the officer's servant?
questions.a: He was very sick, and he was close to dying.

questions.q: What did the officer say Jesus could do?
questions.a: That Jesus only had to say the word, and his servant would get well. Jesus did not even need to come to the house.

questions.q: The officer trusted what Jesus said. What is something Jesus has told us that we can trust?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. It might be “Do not be afraid” or “I am with you always.” Help the child pick one and say it together.

pages.try_this: Make a card that says “Jesus loves you.” Give it to someone, and then pray together for someone who is sick.
